Trump's Russia sanctions waiver eases India's energy woes, lifts trade deal chances
The U.S. administration signaled plans for sanctions waivers permitting Indian refiners to import Russian crude without facing secondary economic penalties. Continued access to discounted Urals crude safeguards gross refining margins for Indian Oil, BPCL, and Reliance Industries while limiting foreign exchange outflows. Urals discount spreads relative to Brent over the next few cargo tenders will confirm whether refinery feedstock costs actually decline.

RBI injects Rs 1 lakh crore as liquidity tightens before festive season
The Reserve Bank of India injected one lakh crore rupees via a variable rate repo auction after the weighted average call rate hit 5.67%, 17 basis points above the policy rate. The liquidity infusion addresses interbank cash deficits before festive currency withdrawals strain banking system liquidity. This prevents short-term borrowing costs and certificate of deposit yields from rising for commercial banks and non-bank lenders.

India-New Zealand FTA to eliminate tariffs on all Indian exports from October 20: DGFT official - ANI News
India and New Zealand finalized a trade agreement eliminating tariffs on all Indian goods entering New Zealand starting October 20. The duty elimination improves price competitiveness for Indian textile exporters, leather goods manufacturers, and generic drugmakers, directly aiding firms like Gokaldas Exports and Welspun Living. Bilateral trade volumes remain modest at around one billion dollars, so the near-term contribution to aggregate corporate revenues will be limited.

Lower switching costs help Indian IT exporters such as Infosys and Tata Consultancy Services contain cloud infrastructure fees when delivering client AI deployments. ‘Data centre in a container’: The multibillion-dollar opportunity and 2 stocks to watch - The Financial Express
Modular containerised units integrate power, cooling, and compute into transportable enclosures, compressing typical data centre construction timelines from eighteen months to a few weeks. In India, decentralized edge infrastructure deployment drives equipment order books for Schneider Electric Infrastructure, Cummins India, and Blue Star across backup power and precision cooling segments. Faster commissioning schedules also reduce working capital lock-in for industrial automation and smart grid projects.

Intense institutional demand confirms the sector-wide valuation rerating underway for domestic defense electronics suppliers, supporting price-to-earnings multiples for peers such as Bharat Electronics, Data Patterns, and Zen Technologies. First-day listing premiums will indicate whether institutional interest translates into durable secondary market ownership.

India sets import quotas for New Zealand apples, kiwifruit under FTA
India introduced phased five-year import quotas for New Zealand kiwifruit, honey, and albumins, while initially barring apple import concessions. The calibrated opening protects domestic farm-gate realizations from sudden supply shocks. Listed cold-chain and logistics operators such as Snowman Logistics may see modest incremental throughput as high-value temperate produce volumes rise under regulated customs tiers.

Sterling hits 17-month high against euro
The British pound reached a 17-month high against the euro, reflecting policy divergence between the Bank of England and the European Central Bank. For Indian IT exporters such as Tata Consultancy Services and Mphasis, sterling strength provides a modest cross-currency translation tailwind on UK revenues. Conversely, European operations of Indian auto-ancillaries face localized margin shifts depending on their euro-to-sterling procurement mismatches.

China vs US vs Europe vs India: Who Leads Clean-Tech Manufacturing in 2026? Major Solar, EV Battery and Wind Factory Investments - GreentechLead
Global manufacturing data projects China will retain over 70% of solar and battery capacity through 2026, despite India's production-linked incentives. Persistent Chinese overcapacity keeps global solar module prices depressed. This dynamic caps operating margins for domestic equipment manufacturers like Premier Energies and Waaree Energies, while directly reducing capital expenditure per megawatt for independent power producers like Tata Power and NTPC Green Energy.

Central Bank of India reports technical glitch in RTGS outward system
Central Bank of India experienced an outward RTGS settlement disruption, confirming no customer financial loss or cybersecurity breach. The technical glitch carries no material impact on earnings or core operations. It matters only if repeated failures attract regulatory audits or capital expenditure directives from the Reserve Bank of India under its technology governance guidelines.

UltraTech Cement Q2 net profit up 21% in September quarter
UltraTech Cement recorded a 21% year-on-year net profit increase, driven by a 14% domestic volume rise to 35.94 million tonnes and consolidated sales reaching ₹23,295 crore. Volume growth and lower energy costs offset subdued realization prices, supporting blended unit EBITDA. The durability of wholesale cement price hikes announced across central and northern markets will determine margin expansion in the subsequent quarter.

Brokerages reiterated positive stances on ICICI Bank and HDFC Bank following second-quarter prints, noting divergent operating performances. ICICI Bank protected its net interest margin and asset quality, sustaining a return on assets above two percent. Conversely, HDFC Bank continues to face margin pressure as it digests merger-related liabilities. The upcoming quarterly credit-deposit ratio will signal whether HDFC Bank can expand lending without sacrificing net interest margins.

Ashish Kacholia buys into this lead recycler. Can the stock overcome margin pressure?
Investor Ashish Kacholia acquired a 2.7 percent stake in Ardee Industries as elevated ocean freight and raw material import costs compress gross margins. Upcoming quarterly filings will confirm whether gross profit margins per ton can stabilize despite persistent import logistics costs.

India notified zero-duty tariff rate quotas for New Zealand kiwifruit priced above 1.80 dollars per kilogram and 40 tonnes of Manuka honey. The policy change has negligible bearing on domestic consumer staples makers like Dabur, given tiny permitted volumes targeted strictly at premium niches. The notification will not materially affect earnings, margins, or domestic market share for listed Indian food and retail companies.

Oil prices fall after Trump waives some Russia sanctions and tariffs - Quartz
Brent crude dropped after the US granted selective waivers on Russian oil sanctions, softening immediate supply-risk premiums across global energy markets. Cheaper crude reduces India's import bill, supporting the rupee while lowering petrochemical input costs for paintmakers and tyre manufacturers. It also widens gross marketing margins on retail fuel for state refiners BPCL, HPCL, and Indian Oil Corporation.
